caption: The drawing is a top-down, colored plan of a large estate labeled “The Ingham Estate — The Blackwell Survey 1860.” The map features paths and roads shown in light brown, winding throughout expansive yellow-green fields. In the lower-central part of the image, there is a large main building, illustrated with gray and red rooftops, surrounded by landscaped grounds. Near this main structure, there are other smaller buildings and fenced-in areas, including rectangular and circular garden plots, some with visible rows suggesting agricultural beds. Trees in various shapes and sizes, colored in shades of green, are scattered throughout the estate, with denser clusters in the bottom left and left edges of the drawing. At the center-left, there is a large circular garden with radial beds, marked by patches of red and pink indicating flowers or plants. Curved and straight pathways traverse the estate, and individual trees or bushes dot the landscape. The upper right corner depicts a light blue body of water, bordered by vegetation. The background outside the estate boundaries is shaded in a salmon or light red-orange color, demarcating the estate’s limits. The drawing is bordered by a simple beige frame, and a small scale bar appears at the bottom right.
title: Thomas Ingham Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
